alerts.name: Cross Site Scripting (Reflected)
alerts.desc: Cross-site Scripting (XSS) is an attack technique that involves echoing attacker-supplied code into a user's browser instance.
alerts.solution:
Phase: Architecture and Design

Use a vetted library or framework that does not allow this weakness to occur or provides constructs that make this weakness easier to avoid.

alerts.name: X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing
alerts.desc: The Anti-MIME-Sniffing header X-Content-Type-Options was not set to 'nosniff'.
alerts.solution: Ensure that the application sets the Content-Type header appropriately, and that it sets the X-Content-Type-Options header to 'nosniff' for all web responses.

alerts.name: Path Traversal
alerts.desc: The Path Traversal attack technique allows an attacker access to files, directories, and commands that potentially reside outside the web document root directory.
alerts.solution: Assume all input is malicious. Use an appropriate security control such as an input validation routine that restricts input to known good values.
